subject: frozen metal pole
title: What If You Licked a Frozen Metal Pole?

scenes.text: What if you licked a frozen metal pole? The cold isn't what traps you.
Your tongue is warm and wet. The moment it touches, the metal starts pulling heat out of it.
Metal moves heat hundreds of times faster than your tongue can replace it.
Within seconds, the saliva on your tongue freezes into the tiny bumps and pits of the metal.
Now ice is gluing you to the pole. Yanking away can tear off the surface of your tongue.
The fix is warm water poured where tongue meets metal. Your own spit was the glue.

description:
What if you licked a frozen metal pole? Metal pulls heat out of your tongue far faster than your body can replace it, so your saliva freezes into the metal's surface and glues you on.
Pulling away can rip skin; warm water poured on the spot melts the ice and frees you.
